notes: Kind of a fall window [t, c]: c = first bar within 26 weeks with BTC.D <= BTC.D(t) - 5; ALT-LED if TOTAL3 (USD) at c >= TOTAL3 at t, else CRASH-LED; ETH-led = ETH/BTC at c > at t (second discriminator, reported, not modelled). The kind is a label property (read only inside [t, c], inside the 26-week horizon), so alt5_26w / crash5_26w carry the same 26-week label lag as fall5_26w in study8_common.walk_forward.

A fall week whose kind cannot be read (TOTAL3 exists from 2017-07-16) is NaN in alt5/crash5 and enters no training label for those targets (it stays a positive of fall5_26w for the generic model): 43 such weeks, all in the 2016-17 waterfall; TOTAL2 (ex BTC) is printed for that episode as a context diagnostic only. The alt/crash models therefore train on slightly fewer positives than the generic one.

Under this definition nearly every fall since 2017 is alt-led (TOTAL3 held or rose while BTC.D fell); crash-led weeks are the Oct 2021 and May-Jun 2022 windows only, so crash5_26w has positives in 2021-22 alone and its AUC is undefined in the other eras ('na'); every by-era crash number and the by-era (c) difference are 2021-22 numbers.

Criterion (c) as written scores the generic model (fixed5 fitted on fall5_26w, unchanged from round 8) against alt5_26w and against crash5_26w on the common rows, where the other kind's positive weeks count as negatives: a correct fall call of the other kind is penalised. The shared-negatives AUC (one kind's positives against the non-fall weeks only) is printed beside it as a diagnostic and is not a criterion.

Bands for (c): 26-week circular block bootstrap of the rows and an episode bootstrap over the FALL episodes with their 26-week run-up (the parent of both labels); draws in which a kind has no positive are dropped and the valid count is printed (n); criterion (c) is 'not identifiable' when a band has fewer than 50 valid draws.

Reassignment null: whole fall episodes (runs of fall5_26w = 1 on the labelled common rows) are relabelled alt-led / crash-led with the real episode counts by majority kind, and the generic model's alt-minus-crash difference is rescored (no refit: the generic model never sees the kind); enumerated exactly when the distinct assignments are at most max(n, 120). The real statistic uses the week-level kind (the criterion); the same statistic under episode-majority labels is printed beside it because the null is episode-pure.

Within-era nulls: dwell-time block permutations of the TARGET's episodes and gaps (study8_honest.perm_blocks / apply_order on the labelled rows of the era, every Y column moved together, whole procedure rerun with every model refitted); an era with no positive of the kind has an empty null (not identifiable); an era is enumerated exactly when its arrangements are at most max(n_within, 120) and the smallest attainable p is 1 / arrangements.

Shifted-target nulls: every target column shifted together by 26+ weeks, every model refitted on the shifted labels, scored on the same rows; the generic model's alt-minus-crash difference has its own shift null (diagnostic). The circular shift moves the NaN kind weeks of the 2016-17 waterfall and the 26-week NaN tail with the labels (the round-9 convention), so a shifted alt5/crash5 draw trains on slightly different rows than the real run; the real row mask is reapplied for scoring.

Within-era nulls keep the dwell structure of the PERMUTED kind only: the other kind's runs sit inside that kind's gap blocks and travel with them, so under the alt-kind null the crash runs (and the parent fall5 run count) can merge or split; fine for (b), which permutes the alt kind.

Shared-negatives AUC, the per-crash-run AUCs, the clustered event counts, the crash-week margin sweep, the size-matched reassignment subsets, the prediction correlation with the reference and the training-positive tags were added at implementation time as diagnostics beside the registered criteria; none enters a criterion's status and 'wouldRead' never replaces the registered content word.

Criterion (c)'s crash side rests on 6 crash-led weeks in 2 episodes (3 runs), all in 2021-22 and all ETH-led, below the 4-episode identifiability gate the plan registered for the alt side only; the as-written gap is carried by the May-Jun 2022 weeks (the Oct 2021 crash-led weeks score like alt weeks), so 'both kinds' is the only reading the sample can give and is not a finding about crashes; a crash-side gate would be a round-11 pre-registration.

Paired bands against the reference (fixed5 on fall5_26w) on alt5 and crash5: study9_candidates.paired_all (26-week block bootstrap pooled and by era, episode bootstrap over the target's episodes with run-up, era-stratified, fresh-start rows).

Readiness rule = BTC within 5% of its true all-time high (study8_honest.ath_drawdown, full BTCUSD history) AND M2 y/y > 0 (6-week publication lag in the loader); its precision on each kind is the share of rule-on weeks that are positives of that kind.

Sub-era decoys (study9_checks): an indicator of the first forward era (1 before 2021-01-01) and a descending time trend, scored on the same rows; a pooled AUC that does not exceed theirs is a level ranking across eras, the era-stratified AUC is the within-era part.

The last complete weekly bar is the last Sunday strictly before the last daily row; the provisional bar is in no feature, label or reading. Every monthly series is lagged by its publication lag in study8_common.load_daily before any feature.

Optional round-10 series on disk at run time: ['CNM2', 'EUM2', 'EURUSD', 'FEDBS', 'GBM2', 'GBPUSD', 'JPM2', 'RRP', 'STABLES', 'TGA', 'USDC.D', 'USDCNY', 'USDJPY']; this module uses none of them (its inputs are BTC.D, TOTAL3, ETHBTC, BTCUSD, USDT.D, M2), so no candidate here depends on an absent series.

Null draw counts are printed beside every p (n!, i.e. fewer than 50, means resolution 1/n, not a p-value; E = enumerated exactly); only the full run's p-values are quotable. Nothing here touches the bot.
